findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the instance.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext inside the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in Terraform state and instance metadata, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata service, state file, or console.

findings.issue_category: public IP exposure of compute instance
findings.description: The instance is launched in aws_subnet.portal_subnet_a, which has map_public_ip_on_launch enabled, directly assigning a public IP to the server and exposing it to the internet in combination with the permissive security group.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing all instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive a public IP address, increasing attack surface without explicit justification per instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true for this subnet as well, automatically exposing any future instances placed here to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest, violating data protection requirements for sensitive or regulated data.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic logs unencrypted at rest.
No public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions are defined for this bucket, leaving the flow log archive without explicit protections against public exposure.
